hotspots.label: Air filter / flame arrestor
hotspots.check: A choked intake starves the engine of air — clean or replace.
hotspots.purpose: Cleans the air entering the engine — a choked filter starves it.

hotspots.label: Throttle plate
hotspots.check: Sticking plate = rough idle or surge at light throttle.
hotspots.purpose: Controls how much air (and fuel) the engine gets.

hotspots.label: Reed valves / manifold
hotspots.check: Stuck reeds (2-stroke) = backfire through the intake.
hotspots.purpose: One-way valves that let the mixture in on 2-strokes; stuck reeds = backfire.

hotspots.label: Intake gaskets / leaks
hotspots.check: Unmetered air leans the mixture — hunt with the engine running.
hotspots.purpose: The gaskets and joints sealing the intake — a leak adds unmetered air.

diagrams.title: Battery System
diagrams.subtitle: Battery dying, dead at the dock

hotspots.label: Battery
hotspots.check: Age (4–5 yrs = replace), voltage (12.6 V+ charged), terminals clean?
hotspots.purpose: Stores starting power and runs the boat\

hotspots.label: Battery switch
hotspots.check: Parasitic draw — something left on the accessory position.
hotspots.purpose: Disconnects the battery; a left-on accessory drains it.

hotspots.label: Fuses / breakers
hotspots.check: Blown fuse = dead circuit. Check before blaming the battery.
hotspots.purpose: Protect each circuit; a blown fuse kills that circuit only.

hotspots.label: Battery wiring
hotspots.check: Loose or corroded = everything acts dead. Tighten and clean.
hotspots.purpose: Carries power from battery to everything; corroded = everything acts dead.

diagrams.title: Bilge System
diagrams.subtitle: Taking on water, pump not clearing

hotspots.label: Drain plug
hotspots.check: The classic. In and tight before launch, checked first when wet.
hotspots.purpose: The drain plug in the hull — the classic leak source.

hotspots.label: Bilge pump
hotspots.check: Turn it on — is it clearing? Then check the float switch.
hotspots.purpose: Pumps water out of the bilge.

hotspots.label: Float switch
hotspots.check: Auto pump not kicking in? A stuck float switch is the usual.
hotspots.purpose: Turns the bilge pump on automatically when water rises.

hotspots.label: Pump hoses
hotspots.check: Split or loose hose = pump runs but water stays in.
hotspots.purpose: Carry bilge water to the discharge fitting.

hotspots.label: Discharge thru-hull
hotspots.check: Blocked outlet = pump works but can\
hotspots.purpose: The hull fitting the pump pushes water out through.

diagrams.title: Charging System
diagrams.subtitle: No charging, battery dies while running

hotspots.label: Alternator / stator
hotspots.check: Voltage should rise to 13.5–14.5 V at 2000+ RPM.
hotspots.purpose: Generates electricity while the engine runs.

hotspots.label: Rectifier / regulator
hotspots.check: Over- or under-charging is usually a dead regulator.
hotspots.purpose: Keeps charging voltage in the safe 13.5–14.5 V range.

hotspots.label: Charging wiring
hotspots.check: Loose or corroded connections kill charging silently.
hotspots.purpose: Carries charging current from the engine to the battery.

hotspots.label: Battery
hotspots.check: Only as good as its connections — clean and tight, 12.6 V+ when charged.
hotspots.purpose: Stores starting power and runs accessories when the engine is off.

hotspots.label: Water pickup
hotspots.check: Blocked intake? Weeds, bag or mud starve the whole system.
hotspots.purpose: Scoops lake water into the cooling system — a blocked intake starves everything downstream.

hotspots.label: Water pump / impeller
hotspots.check: Weak or no telltale stream = impeller is the first suspect.
hotspots.purpose: The rubber pump that pushes cooling water through the engine.

hotspots.label: Cooling hoses
hotspots.check: Collapsed or kinked hose — classic at high RPM.
hotspots.purpose: Carry cooling water between the pump, block and tell-tale.

hotspots.label: Thermostat
hotspots.check: Idle-only overheating often = thermostat stuck shut.
hotspots.purpose: Regulates engine temperature — stuck shut, the engine overheats at idle.

hotspots.label: Engine block / head
hotspots.check: Heavy white smoke = water in combustion. Stop before it warps.
hotspots.purpose: The engine casting itself; water jackets inside carry heat away.

hotspots.label: Telltale stream
hotspots.check: Should be a steady stream at idle. Weak or none = pump problem.
hotspots.purpose: The small "pee hole" stream that shows the pump is actually working.

diagrams.title: Exhaust System
diagrams.subtitle: Smoke color, water in exhaust, backpressure

hotspots.label: Manifold / risers
hotspots.check: Corroded riser = water in the cylinders. Heavy white smoke = stop.
hotspots.purpose: Routes exhaust out; corroded risers can let water into cylinders.

hotspots.label: Water injection / muffler
hotspots.check: Blocked water jacket = engine runs hot and loud.
hotspots.purpose: Cools the exhaust with water so the engine and boat stay quiet and safe.

hotspots.label: Exhaust outlet
hotspots.check: Restricted outlet = backpressure, poor power, overheat risk.
hotspots.purpose: The exhaust discharge; a restriction raises backpressure.

hotspots.label: Exhaust gaskets
hotspots.check: Exhaust smell in the boat = leaking gasket, a CO hazard.
hotspots.purpose: Seal the exhaust joints — a leak can push fumes into the boat.

diagrams.title: Freshwater System
diagrams.subtitle: No flow, weak pressure, air locks

hotspots.label: Freshwater tank
hotspots.check: Empty or vent blocked = no flow no matter how hard the pump works.
hotspots.purpose: Stores the drinking/wash water.

hotspots.label: Water pump
hotspots.check: No power (fuse) or dead pump = nothing at the tap.
hotspots.purpose: Pressurizes the freshwater lines to the taps.

hotspots.label: Filter / strainer
hotspots.check: Blocked filter = weak pressure. Clean it first.
hotspots.purpose: Strains the water before it reaches the taps.

hotspots.label: Faucets / lines
hotspots.check: Air lock = open a tap to bleed. Leaks = check the fittings.
hotspots.purpose: The taps and plumbing the water flows through.

hotspots.label: Fuel tank
hotspots.check: Vent open? Vapor-locked tanks won\
hotspots.purpose: Stores the fuel; needs a working vent to let air in as fuel leaves.

hotspots.label: Tank vent
hotspots.check: Blocked vent starves the engine — it leans out and surges.
hotspots.purpose: Lets air into the tank as fuel is used — blocked vents vapor-lock the system.

hotspots.label: Fuel line
hotspots.check: Cracked or pinched line — prime suspect for fuel smell.
hotspots.purpose: Carries fuel from the tank to the engine.

hotspots.label: Primer bulb
hotspots.check: Must pump firm. Soft = air leak or empty pickup.
hotspots.purpose: Hand pump that primes fuel up to the engine; firm = fuel is there.

hotspots.label: Filter / water separator
hotspots.check: Milky fuel = water. Drain it — it collects here first.
hotspots.purpose: Traps water and debris before they reach the carb or injectors.

hotspots.label: Carb / injectors
hotspots.check: Dirty carb or injectors = stalls, rough idle, black smoke.
hotspots.purpose: Mixes fuel and air for combustion.

hotspots.label: Gear set
hotspots.check: Grinding or slipping gears = wear in the gearcase.
hotspots.purpose: Transfers engine power to the prop at the right ratio.

hotspots.label: Shift dog / clutch
hotspots.check: A worn shift dog jumps out of gear under load.
hotspots.purpose: Locks the drive into forward/neutral/reverse; worn dogs slip under load.

hotspots.label: Drive shaft
hotspots.check: Bent or worn shaft = vibration that\
hotspots.purpose: Carries power down into the gearcase.

hotspots.label: Gear oil
hotspots.check: Milky = water got in. Metal flakes = gears wearing. Both bad.
hotspots.purpose: Lubricates the gears; milky oil means water got in.

hotspots.label: Spark plugs
hotspots.check: Fouled or worn plugs = no fire. Check gap and condition.
hotspots.purpose: Ignite the fuel-air mixture — fouled or worn plugs mean no fire.

hotspots.label: Coils / packs
hotspots.check: Weak spark under load = failing coil. Test with a spark tester.
hotspots.purpose: Step up voltage to fire the plugs.

hotspots.label: Kill switch / lanyard
hotspots.check: The #1 "won\
hotspots.purpose: Safety lanyard switch that kills the ignition when pulled.

hotspots.label: Ignition wiring
hotspots.check: Corroded or chafed wires = intermittent no-spark.
hotspots.purpose: Carries trigger and spark signals; chafed wire = intermittent no-spark.

hotspots.label: Livewell pump
hotspots.check: Running but no flow = worn impeller or air lock.
hotspots.purpose: Circulates fresh water through the livewell to keep fish alive.

hotspots.label: Water intake
hotspots.check: Weeds or debris on the pickup = no water in the tank.
hotspots.purpose: The water pickup feeding the livewell pump.

hotspots.label: Overflow / drain
hotspots.check: Blocked overflow = tank won\
hotspots.purpose: Lets the tank drain and set its level.

hotspots.label: Aerator / recirculation
hotspots.check: Dead aerator = fish suffocate in a "live" well.
hotspots.purpose: Recirculates and aerates the water when the boat is stationary.

diagrams.title: Lubrication System
diagrams.subtitle: Low oil pressure, oil warnings, burning oil

hotspots.label: Oil level / pan
hotspots.check: Low oil = the #1 cause of pressure warnings. Check the dipstick.
hotspots.purpose: The oil supply in the pan — low oil is the #1 pressure warning cause.

hotspots.label: Oil pump
hotspots.check: Worn pump or relief valve = pressure drops when hot.
hotspots.purpose: Pressurizes oil to the bearings; worn pumps lose pressure when hot.

hotspots.label: Oil filter
hotspots.check: Clogged filter or pickup screen starves the pump.
hotspots.purpose: Strains the oil; a clogged filter starves the pump.

hotspots.label: Pressure sender / alarm
hotspots.check: False alarm possible — but never assume. Verify with a gauge.
hotspots.purpose: The sensor that trips the oil-pressure warning.

diagrams.title: Navigation Lights
diagrams.subtitle: Dead lights, one side only, running dark

hotspots.label: Bow light
hotspots.check: Dead bulb/LED or corroded socket — swap to test.
hotspots.purpose: Red/green running light at the bow.

hotspots.label: Stern light
hotspots.check: One light works, other doesn\
hotspots.purpose: White stern light completing the running-light pattern.

hotspots.label: Light switch
hotspots.check: Check the switch and its fuse before pulling any light.
hotspots.purpose: The switch that powers the nav-light circuit.

hotspots.label: Wiring / ground
hotspots.check: Corroded connector or bad ground = intermittent or half-lit.
hotspots.purpose: Carries power to the lights; bad grounds kill one side.

hotspots.label: Prop hub
hotspots.check: Spun hub = rubber slips under load. Engine revs, boat doesn\
hotspots.purpose: The rubber-cushioned centre that drives the prop; a spun hub slips under load.

hotspots.label: Prop blades
hotspots.check: Bent or dinged blades = vibration. Inspect all of them.
hotspots.purpose: Push the boat through the water; bent blades vibrate.

hotspots.label: Shear pin / key
hotspots.check: Sheared pin (older outboards) = no drive at all.
hotspots.purpose: Sacrificial pin (older outboards) that breaks to protect the drive.

hotspots.label: Shift cable
hotspots.check: Out of adjustment or broken = the control moves, the drive doesn\
hotspots.purpose: Carries shift motion from the control to the drive.

hotspots.label: Linkage arm
hotspots.check: Bent or worn arm = sloppy or missed shifts.
hotspots.purpose: Connects the cable to the shift mechanism.

hotspots.label: Neutral safety switch
hotspots.purpose: Safety switch that blocks cranking in gear.

diagrams.title: Steering System
diagrams.subtitle: Hard to steer, stiff, no response

hotspots.label: Helm / wheel
hotspots.check: Wheel spins free but the engine doesn\
hotspots.purpose: The wheel and control at the helm.

hotspots.label: Steering cable
hotspots.check: Corroded or binding cable — common on boats that sit unused.
hotspots.purpose: Carries steering motion from the helm to the engine.

hotspots.label: Steering fluid
hotspots.check: Hydraulic steering? Low fluid is the common one.
hotspots.purpose: Hydraulic fluid for power/hydraulic steering.

hotspots.label: Steering tube / tilt
hotspots.check: Stiff swivel = grease the tube before blaming anything else.
hotspots.purpose: The swivel tube the engine tilts on; stiff = needs grease.

diagrams.title: Trailer Wiring
diagrams.subtitle: Lights out, flickering, one side dead

hotspots.label: Connector plug
hotspots.check: Corroded pins = half the trailer faults. Clean and test first.
hotspots.purpose: Connects the trailer to the tow vehicle\

hotspots.label: Wiring harness
hotspots.check: Broken wire at a flex point (near the tongue) = intermittent.
hotspots.purpose: The wiring run along the trailer frame.

hotspots.label: Ground
hotspots.check: Bad ground = flicker or one side only. The classic trailer fault.
hotspots.purpose: The return path for trailer lights; bad ground = flicker.

hotspots.label: Trailer lights
hotspots.check: Sealed LED unit dead = replace the unit, don\
hotspots.purpose: The trailer\

hotspots.label: Trim pump / motor
hotspots.check: Hear the pump run? If yes, it\
hotspots.purpose: Hydraulic pump that raises and lowers the drive.

hotspots.label: Hydraulic fluid
hotspots.check: Low fluid = slow or no movement. Top up with the right spec.
hotspots.purpose: The hydraulic fluid the trim system runs on.

hotspots.label: Trim switch
hotspots.check: Switch clicks but nothing moves = check the switch and relay.
hotspots.purpose: The helm switch that runs the trim pump.

hotspots.label: Relay / fuse
hotspots.check: Dead trim = blown fuse or relay first. Cheap and common.
hotspots.purpose: Switches power to the trim motor; a dead relay is a common cheap fix.

hotspots.label: Impeller
hotspots.check: The rubber heart of the cooling system. Weak stream = replace it.
hotspots.purpose: The rubber heart of the cooling system — the most common overheat cause.

hotspots.label: Pump housing
hotspots.check: Scored housing leaks pressure — the impeller can\
hotspots.purpose: The pump body the impeller spins in; scoring leaks pressure.

hotspots.label: Wear plate
hotspots.check: Grooved wear plate = lost pump pressure.
hotspots.purpose: The wear plate the impeller runs against.

hotspots.label: Drive key
hotspots.check: Sheared key = pump runs dry and silently. Never run it dry.
hotspots.purpose: Small key that drives the impeller; sheared = pump runs dry silently.

Overheating.start: Weak or no tell-tale stream? Impeller is the first suspect.

outboard: Water inlet blocked by weeds or plastic.
jet: Wear ring damage causing cavitation heat.
default: Running too shallow.
Plastic bag on intake.
High RPM with weak water flow.

Overheating.ifNotResolved: Shut down immediately if alarm sounds — overheating can warp heads or seize pistons.

No charging.start: Voltage dropping while running? Alternator or stator issue.

default: Battery old or sulfated.
High electrical load (pumps, lights).

No charging.ifNotResolved: If voltage drops below 11.5V underway, shut down unnecessary loads.

Battery dying.start: Voltage sag when cranking? Battery or connections.

default: High load (pumps, lights).
Battery near end of life.

Battery dying.ifNotResolved: If voltage drops below 11V, stop cranking.

default: Rudder fouled.
Trim tab bent.

Hard to steer.ifNotResolved: If steering locks completely, stop immediately.

default: Water in fuel.
Loose fuel line.
Debris on prop.
Engine mount loose.

Water in fuel.start: Drain the water-separating filter — that\'s where water collects first.

default: Condensation in the tank over winter or long storage.
Bad fuel from a station with old tanks.
Vent cap missing its seal — rain gets in.
Water-separating filter overdue for a change.

Water in fuel.ifNotResolved: If the engine runs rough after draining, the tank may need pumping out — don\'t just add dry-gas and hope.

Smoke — white / blue / black.start: Match the color: white = water, blue = oil, black = fuel.

outboard: White: cold-start condensation is normal; heavy white = water in combustion (head gasket).
Blue: oil burning (2-stroke mix too rich, or worn rings).
Black: rich fuel — choke stuck, carb dirty, or fuel pressure too high.
default: White: water in combustion — head gasket or cracked block (serious).
Blue: oil burning — worn rings, valve guides, or overfilled oil.
Black: too much fuel — choke, carb, or injectors.

Smoke — white / blue / black.ifNotResolved: Heavy white smoke after warm-up = water in the engine. Stop — that\'s an expensive fix if you run it.

Fuel smell in cabin.start: Vent the compartment immediately and don\'t run anything electrical.

default: Fuel line or fitting leak under the floor.
Vent hose disconnected or clogged.
Carburetor bowl leaking or flooding.
Fill overflow left fuel in the bilge.

Fuel smell in cabin.ifNotResolved: Any fuel in the bilge is a fire risk — find and fix it before starting the engine again.

Air intake problems.start: Check the air filter first — a choked intake starves the engine of air.

default: Clogged air filter or flame arrestor.
Restricted intake / vent — engine runs rich or won\'t rev clean.
Reed valves (2-stroke) or throttle plate sticking.
Air leak after the filter — unmetered air leans the mixture.

Air intake problems.ifNotResolved: A backfire through the intake often means an air leak or stuck reed — get it checked before running hard.

Oil pressure problems.start: Low oil pressure warning = shut down NOW and check the dipstick before restarting.

default: Low oil level — top up, but find out where it went.
Clogged oil filter or pickup screen.
Worn oil pump or relief valve.
Wrong oil weight or old oil too thin when hot.

Oil pressure problems.ifNotResolved: Running with low oil pressure can destroy the bottom end — if the warning stays on, get it towed and diagnosed.

Freshwater problems.start: No water flow? Check the tank level and pump first — the pump primes the whole system.

default: Tank empty or pump not getting power (fuse/breaker).
Pump runs but no flow — blocked filter or kinked line.
Air lock in the line — open a faucet to bleed it.
Low battery voltage makes the pump run weak.

Freshwater problems.ifNotResolved: A pump that runs but delivers nothing is usually a blockage — check the filter before replacing the pump.

Livewell problems.start: Is the pump running but no water circulating? Check the intake and the pump first.

default: Intake or pickup blocked by weeds or debris.
Pump impeller worn or pump not priming.
Overflow or drain line blocked — tank won\'t fill or drain.
Aerator/recirculation pump dead (fuse or wiring).

Livewell problems.ifNotResolved: Fish in a dead livewell is a spoiled trip — fix the flow before you rely on it.

Navigation lights not working.start: Bulbs vs power: check the switch and fuse before pulling any light.

default: Blown fuse or tripped breaker for the nav-light circuit.
Dead bulb or LED fixture — test by swapping.
Corroded socket or connector (the classic on trailers).
Bad ground — one light works, the other doesn\'t.

Navigation lights not working.ifNotResolved: Running dark at dusk is dangerous and illegal in most waters — fix the lights before heading out at night.

Trailer wiring problems.start: Test the plug with the tow vehicle lights ON — half the faults are at the connector.

default: Corroded plug pins or loose connection at the connector.
Broken wire in the harness (flex point near the tongue).
Bad ground — lights flicker or work one side only.
Faulty bulbs on the trailer side (sealed LED = replace unit).

Trailer wiring problems.ifNotResolved: A trailer that shows no brake lights is a road hazard — fix the ground and connector before towing.

Alarm / beeping.start: Continuous beep = shut down NOW. That\'s overheat or low oil pressure.
Alarm / beeping.ifNotResolved: Any alarm you can\'t identify: safe stop, then check the manual\'s alarm chart before running again.

Taking on water.start: Drain plug — the classic. Check it first, then the bilge pump.
Taking on water.ifNotResolved: Water rising faster than the bilge pump clears it? Call for help NOW and share your position.

Smells like gas.start: Stop, shut everything off, and don\'t touch anything electrical until you find it.
Smells like gas.ifNotResolved: Strong fuel smell while running = get off the water and vent the compartment before anything else.
